title: Inconsistent errors and warnings for shadowed global identifiers
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.dev [220b0b2f7], 4.6.stable, 4.4.1.stable.

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop - Intel i7-12700H (20 threads)

### Issue description

Local variable names only have `SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER` warnings, but member variable names have `SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER` warnings plus unique errors, which is inconsistent.

Not sure if this is intended, or if those unique warnings were legacy code before `SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER` existed.

Discovered this issue when working on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106984, but I forgot to report it back then.

### Steps to reproduce

Attach this script to a Node and run the scene.
Test each variable name one at a time.
```gdscript
extends Node

# Parse Error: The member "int" cannot have the same name as a builtin type. # <-- here
# Warning: Variable "int" has no static type. (UNTYPED_DECLARATION)
# Warning: The variable "int" has the same name as a built-in type. (SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER)
var int = 0

# Error: The member "Node" shadows a native class. # <-- here
# Warning: Variable "Node" has no static type. (UNTYPED_DECLARATION)
# Warning: The variable "Node" has the same name as a native class. (SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER)
var Node = null

# Warning: Variable "abs" has no static type. (UNTYPED_DECLARATION)
# Warning: The variable "abs" has the same name as a built-in function. (SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER)
var abs

func local_method() -> void:
    # Warning: Variable "int" has no static type. (UNTYPED_DECLARATION)
    # Warning: The variable "int" has the same name as a built-in type. (SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER)
    var int = 0
    print(int) # 0
```
